key_reasoning.reason: Touches three components across two layers: the NSIS installer hooks (preinstall silent-uninstall, postuninstall PATH cleanup), the app_updater.rs command module (platform-specific launch_installer for Windows /S silent spawn vs. macOS DMG bundle-swap, manifest/platform-entry resolution), and the shared AppState struct in state.rs (new latest_manifest cache field) — touching a core shared utility struct is what pushes this past a single self-contained component.

Self-update/auto-install surface: the installer silently uninstalls the prior version via a registry-read + ExecWait before install, and download_and_install saves and launches a downloaded binary with no checksum or signature verification — explicitly flagged in-code as a deliberate, tracked gap. Existing rollback logic (staged/old bundle rename with fallback) and unit test coverage (dmg swap, version compare, platform entry) offset some of this, but the missing integrity check on an auto-executed installer is a real security-sensitive gap, so this is scored above the 'well-established pattern' band.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped: touches core shared utility (AppState.latest_manifest in state.rs) alongside the installer-hook and command-module changes.
Technical Risk bumped: security-sensitive self-update path (silent NSIS uninstall/install, no checksum/signature verification on the downloaded installer binary before execution).
